setup_notes: Fork main fast-forwarded to upstream and pushed. There is no --stats flag in this build, so per-stage timings come from the debug build's --trace output (summarised by stages.py). The exploration subagent ran hypothesis.sh itself, so the counter shows 2 for this first hypothesis.

hypotheses.title: Stage 6 re-checks every inferred-parameter (arrow) lambda against its expected type with a cold semtypes context, repeating stage 5's check
hypotheses.issue: Stage 5 (resolveInferredLambdaFunctionExpr) builds an arrow lambda's function type from the expected type and already checks IsSubtype(fnType, expectedType), reporting an error if it fails. Stage 6 (analysis validateLambdaFunction -> validateResolvedType) checks IsSubtype(lambdaType, expected) again. calls.go validateCallArg passes the parameter type as expected. Three things make the stage-6 repeat expensive. First, it runs in the package-wide semtypes.Context created by analysis.Analyze, which has none of stage 5's memoised results. Second, each lambda's function type is built from fresh atoms (new ListDefinition/FunctionDefinition), so the full function/list BDD emptiness check (functionPathIsEmpty -> list Diff/IsEmpty -> internBddNodeKey) runs from scratch for every lambda. Third, stage 6 walks functions serially, so the cost goes straight onto wall time. On the reproducer (20k arrow lambdas passed to user-defined higher-order functions) stage 6 takes 489 ms, almost all of it in this check. Pitfall: explicitly typed lambdas are checked against their expected type only in stage 6, so that check must stay. Skipping it for all lambdas breaks 10-function/explicit-lambda-expected-type-2-e.bal, 10-isolated/explicit-lambda-expected-type-1-e.bal and 10-bug/anon-isolated-expected-e.bal. Also, stage 5's inference type is not always identical to stage 6's expected type. For dependently-typed and opaque langlib functions, stage 6 uses the monomorphized parameter type, while stage 5 uses the generic type or a callback type built inside the monomorphizer. So an unconditional skip for inferred lambdas cannot be proven safe on every path.

reproducer.generator:
# Generates a single-module Ballerina program with many inferred-type lambdas
# (arrow functions) passed to user-defined higher-order functions.
# usage: python3 gen_lambda.py <num_functions> <lambdas_per_function> <out.bal>
import sys
nf = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 400
nl = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 50
path = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "/tmp/perfhunt/H1/lambda.bal"
out = ["import ballerina/io;", "",
       "type Fn1 function (int) returns int;",
       "type Fn3 function (int, string, float) returns int;",
       "type Fn4 function (int, int, string, boolean) returns int;",
       "",
       "function apply1(Fn1 f, int v) returns int => f(v);",
       "function apply3(Fn3 f, int v) returns int => f(v, \"s\", 1.5);",
       "function apply4(Fn4 f, int v) returns int => f(v, v, \"t\", true);",
       ""]
for i in range(nf):
    out.append(f"function f{i}(int x) returns int {{")
    out.append("    int s = 0;")
    for j in range(nl):
        k = j % 3
        if k == 0:
            out.append(f"    s += apply1(a => a + {j}, x);")
        elif k == 1:
            out.append(f"    s += apply3((a, b, c) => a + b.length() + <int>c + {j}, x);")
        else:
            out.append(f"    s += apply4((a, b, c, d) => d ? a * b + {j} : c.length(), x);")
    out.append("    return s;")
    out.append("}")
    out.append("")
out.append("public function main() {")
out.append("    io:println(f0(1));")
out.append("}")
open(path, "w").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")

hypotheses.fix_approach: Stage 5 records the expected type the lambda was inferred from and checked against. The prototype stores it in a new field, BLangLambdaFunction.InferredFrom, set by setLambdaInferredFrom only on non-ephemeral (non-trial) resolution, right after setNodeType. In stage 6, for inferred-parameter lambdas with a recorded InferredFrom, the analysis first checks IsSubtype(InferredFrom, expected). If that holds, the expensive lambda check is skipped: by transitivity, lambdaType <= InferredFrom <= expected. If it does not hold, the original validateResolvedType runs unchanged, so diagnostics stay identical by construction. The InferredFrom-vs-expected check is cheap because the two types usually share their atoms, often being the very same parameter type, so the subtype check short-circuits. A cleaner final fix could have stage 6 trust stage 5 outright where the expected types provably match (user-defined functions). Alternatively, stage 6 could reuse stage 5's semtypes context or memo instead of storing a type on the AST node. Keep the full check for explicitly typed lambdas. make test passes; no locking changes.

notes: Two leads were seen during exploration but not pursued. (1) In multi-module projects, file parsing appears serialised (projects/ documentContext.parse, out of scope; the 215 parse spans in corpus/bench/09-bench/huge-project-v do not overlap, about 4.7 s of 22 s). (2) semtypes/env.go typeAtom keys atomTable by atomic-type pointer, so structurally equal atoms never deduplicate.
